The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of multiple-wavelength data from the L-III edge of a heavy-atom derivative, in conjunction with the maximum-likelihood phasing method, is a viable and efficient approach to solving the phase problem in the case of a protein with a single anomalous scatterer.
the combination of multiple-wavelength anomlaous dispersion and maximum-likelihood methods is a powerful combination for solving the phase problem in protein crystallography.
